purpose: Agent-readable artifact contract for the R3.0-002 multi-slice workflow: scenario map, topology decision record, and protection IRI suggestion handover. Mechanical only; semantic quality is judged by the Coordinator, the user interview, and R3.0-006.

artifact_locations.note: These are run-workspace process artifacts, not platform storage. A missing, non-JSON, symlinked, or escaping path is rejected without touching anything outside the run directory.

rules: the artifact's top-level field set is closed and is exactly schema_version, the two identity_fields, and the six required_sections; `maintainer` (and every other key of this contract object, such as rules) is contract metadata describing who maintains the artifact, never an artifact field, and writing it into scenario-map.json is rejected as map_schema_mismatch top-level fields drift
slices is non-empty; every field is a non-empty string; slice_id values are unique
each shared_terms entry has term, used_by_slices, and exactly one owner_slice inside the slice list; notes is optional; a term registered more than once is rejected
each cross_slice_dependencies entry has from_slice and to_slice inside the slice list, a non-empty direction, and a non-empty connection_points list
each cross-slice competency question has question_id, question, and spans_slices of at least two known slices
explicit_unknowns may be empty; each entry has topic, needed_from, and status
adjustments may be empty; each entry records change and approved_by_coordinator
topology_decision_ref is empty until the decision record exists, then exactly topology-decision.json

topology_decision.timing: Recorded before the first real apply; while it is missing or structurally incomplete, the independent platform MCP gate stays closed and rejects every platform call, including reads. That is expected behavior: repair the artifact from the typed reason code sent to Coordinator and wait for the next Runner re-check; do not retry platform calls.
rules: at least three options and always the three required option_ids; custom options may be appended

each options entry has exactly the two option_fields: option_id is a non-empty string, and assessment is an object whose keys are exactly the six dimensions listed above, each with a non-empty value; the dimensions are assessment keys, never an option-level dimensions container (a wrong option shape is reported as topology_schema_mismatch)

every option assesses all six dimensions with non-empty values; the dimensions are concept cohesion, relation density, reuse, permission boundary, change cadence, and cross-domain query, never table count or team count
selecting single_ontology does not waive the comparison: the full three-option, six-dimension record is still required
selected_option must be one of the listed options and rationale must be non-empty

R3.0-006 additive optional field ontology_plan: must be absent when selected_option is single_ontology, required for every other selection; value is a mechanical list [{name, slice_ids}] with at least two entries, non-empty unique names, and every scenario-map slice assigned to at least one planned Ontology, with a logical slice allowed to be served by more than one planned Ontology (shared core plus domain topology; slice references close against the scenario map's slice list)
at least two planned Ontologies
name values are non-empty and unique
slice_ids is a non-empty list of distinct slice_ids of the current scenario map
every scenario-map slice belongs to at least one planned Ontology; a slice may be served by more than one planned Ontology
the artifact's field set is closed and is exactly the `fields` list; `maintainer` is contract metadata describing who maintains the artifact, never an artifact field
iri is one non-empty absolute IRI; dangling IRIs for resources not yet created are allowed
target_protection_set is existing:<id> or new:<name>
proposing_slice must be a slice of the current scenario map
format only: the decision to protect, and every execution failure, follows the existing R3.0-004 protection-set contract

execution.multi_ontology_batches: One Modeling Batch binds exactly one Ontology. A multi-Ontology topology means at least one batch per Ontology, applied by Protocol in scenario-map dependency order; dry_run then apply_atomic per batch; no cross-batch atomicity is required or provided.
execution.protection_sets: Protection sets are Project-level, may span Ontologies, and must never drive the Ontology split. Protection-set changes and ontology publication are two independent operations and are never part of the same Modeling Batch. Protecting target IRIs before creating the resources is the recommended order, not a platform constraint.
execution.order: Slices run serially in scenario-map dependency order; any slice-set or order adjustment must be recorded in scenario-map adjustments and approved by Coordinator.
